//: The boundary between the harness and the product it happens to guard.
Written 2026-09-11, before any attempt to extract a reusable template, because
a generator built without this would copy files by guesswork and nobody would
notice which ones were wrong. Every script and guard suite on disk must appear
in exactly one tier below; harness-boundary.spec.ts refuses any that does not.
The tiers are about what happens to a file when it is taken to another project,
not about what it does here.
Copied verbatim. Mentions nothing about this product, and would run in any
repository that has git, node and a verify.sh. Seven of these are protected
files, so a template must ship them as copies rather than as imports: the
commit gate hashes them and the witness job runs them in place.
Copied, and then reads its constants from harness.config.json rather than
carrying this project's. Each entry names what has to move out. Until that
file exists these still work, because every constant below is currently a
literal in the script.
The suites that fired at these in link-shortener (coverage-floor, docs-drift,
migrations, ci-workflow, …) asserted that repository's documents and structure
and did not travel. This repository has none of its own yet; the tier stays,
empty, so the next one written has a place to be classified.

scripts/check-environment.mjs: whether Docker is needed at all
scripts/check-feature-list.mjs: the commits exempt from one-closure-per-commit, which were another repository's
scripts/check-work-budget.mjs: the number of tool calls a session may make before it is asked to stop
scripts/check-verify.mjs: the path it writes the deliberate error into
the step list, read from verify.sh rather than carried
scripts/progress.mjs: the contracts package path in its template

//: Not copied. In link-shortener this tier held the guards that belong to a URL
shortener — reserved-paths, smoke-deploy, layer-boundaries — and they stayed
there as worked examples of what a project adds to the harness rather than
as part of it. This repository is the harness alone and has no product, so
the tier is empty; harness-boundary.spec.ts refuses a file on disk that is
in no tier, which is what keeps it from quietly filling up.
What the copied scripts need from npm, which this manifest did not record
until 2026-09-11 and the generated project could not run `inbox.mjs` for.
Packages, never versions. A version here would be a second copy of what
package.json already says, and two copies drift: the generator hardcoded
js-yaml ^4 while this repository had ^5, so a new project would have got a
different major of the library the script was written against. The
generator resolves each name against package.json — or harness.versions.json
for what this repository does not itself use — at generation time, and
harness-boundary.spec.ts refuses a name that is not there to resolve.

scripts.//: Per copied script, what it imports at runtime. Nothing else may be listed, and nothing imported may be left out.

//: What any project running this gate needs regardless of what it is: the
steps call eslint, tsc and jest by name. A project that swaps one of
these swaps a step with it, which is a change to verify.sh and so a
person's decision.

onlyWith.//: Named so the generator can leave them out — the dependency and the script itself. `pg` in a project with no database is a dependency nothing imports, and migrate.mjs, which imports it, would be a script the typecheck cannot pass.

//: What a scaffolded application needs, beyond the toolchain. Chosen in the
CLI, so a project that takes neither pays for neither.
Versions are resolved the same way as everything else here — by name, never
recorded in this file. In link-shortener they came from apps/*/package.json;
this repository has no applications of its own, so they come from
harness.versions.json, which holds exactly the names no package.json here can
give a version for. A name recorded here that neither can resolve is refused,
as it is for the scripts.
Harness files that are not scripts, listed so a generator has the whole set
in one place. `verify.sh`, the CI workflow and .claude/settings.json are
protected: a session may not edit them here, and a generator writes them
into a new project rather than editing them in this one.
`seeded` is what the generator writes fresh for a new project. In
link-shortener it also named four more documents under docs/; the generator
does not write those, and this repository does not have them. CONTRIBUTING.md
and docs/INVARIANTS.md travel as copies, under `core`; docs/DOMAIN_RULES.md is
written as a template, and AGENTS.md tells the new project to fill it in.
`product` is empty here for the reason the product tier above is. security-check.md was product-tier in link-shortener and is general now, so it travels.
verify-log/ is not seeded: git keeps no empty directory, and the first gate run creates it. check-attestation.mjs refuses a project with no run on record, which is the state a project is born in.
